chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim ibn Hakim, from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Surely, the Trustworthy Spirit Jibril informed me from my Lord, Blessed and Exalted: A soul does not die until its sustenance has been depleted. So fear Allah, and beautify your pursuit of livelihood. And know that sustenance is of two types: sustenance that you pursue, and sustenance that pursues you. So pursue your sustenance lawfully, for indeed you will consume it lawfully if you pursue it through its proper channels, but if you do not pursue it through its proper channels, you will consume it unlawfully. It is your sustenance, and you cannot but consume it.

key_terms.الروح الامين: Al-Ruh al-Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit) - title of the Archangel Jibril (Gabriel)
key_terms.الطلب: Al-Talab (the pursuit/seeking) - the effort to earn livelihood
key_terms.حرام: Haram (unlawful/forbidden) - means of earning that violate Islamic law
key_terms.حلال: Halal (lawful/permissible) - means and channels of earning that conform to Islamic law
key_terms.رزق: Rizq (sustenance/provision) - divinely allotted livelihood that every soul must consume in its entirety before death

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about sustenance (rizq) and lawful livelihood in al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through a chain from al-Shaykh al-Saduq through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), addresses the pre-determined nature of sustenance (rizq). The Prophet relays a divine message delivered by the Archangel Jibril (Gabriel), assuring that no soul departs this world until its allotted sustenance has been fully consumed. The hadith was delivered as a public address to the faithful community, teaching them that since sustenance is guaranteed, they should pursue it through lawful means rather than resorting to forbidden methods. The Prophet categorizes sustenance into two types: that which one actively seeks, and that which comes to one by divine decree. The emphasis is on pursuing livelihood through permissible channels (halal), warning that if one does not pursue it through proper means, they will still consume their allotted portion but bear the sin of unlawful consumption (haram).
